reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, multiple measured technical, acquisition, and site factors are significantly associated with the candidate-consensus geometry: tissue source site (R-squared 0.345, q=0.0025, with non-significant PERMDISP), CT phase (0.154, q=0.0025, with significant PERMDISP), slice thickness (0.136, q=0.002), z-spacing (0.142, q=0.002), manufacturer (0.059, q=0.0067, significant PERMDISP), pixel spacing (0.019, q=0.035), and study year (0.029, q=0.004). Kernel and scanner model do not survive correction (q=0.054) and their PERMDISP is not estimable due to sparse levels. These are partition-wide associations, not causal contributions, and they indicate that measured site and acquisition factors remain plausible partition-level alternative explanations for the observed structure. PERMANOVA and PERMDISP and the continuous distance-regression p-values belong to separate BH families and are not combined.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This partition-scope confounder picture is consistent with the prior set-scope confounder reports, which found broad technical/acquisition associations for K3_C0002 and more selective associations for K3_C0001 and K3_C0003. Partition-level associations must not be promoted to candidate-specific confounding; the set-scope reports remain the appropriate source for candidate-specific alternative explanations.
limitations: Association is not causation; no covariate adjustment or persistence-after-adjustment is demonstrated.
Nonsignificant factors (kernel, scanner model) do not establish absence of confounding.
PERMDISP is not estimable for kernel and scanner model because some levels have single observations; sparse contingency cells widen uncertainty.
Manufacturer is highly imbalanced (Philips n=3), limiting inference for that level.
Partition-scope evidence describes the partition as a whole and must not be presented as candidate-specific confounding.

limitations: Enrichment is relative to the rest of the current partition (rest_n=75), which combines the other two candidate sets and may be heterogeneous.
